region.text: Misiones, claimed by Paraguay from 1838

'In 1830 Argentine military forces from Corrientes Province took control of Misiones'; 'In 1838, Paraguay occupied Misiones, claiming the area'; 'In 1865, Paraguayan forces invaded Misiones again'. region.text: the new Buenos Aires frontier land of Cliopatria's 1840 shape

region.text: Buenos Aires province, which became the State of Buenos Aires

ledger.note: 11 September 1852: Buenos Aires secedes. The State of Buenos Aires arose from the 'overthrow of the Argentine Confederation government in the Province of Buenos Aires on 11 September 1852'; Urquiza had defeated Rosas at Caseros on 3 February 1852.
1853: the Confederation's capital moves from Buenos Aires to Parana. Infobox: capitals 'Buenos Aires (1831-1853), then Parana (1853-1861)'; the Constitution was sanctioned on 1 May 1853.

region.text: Buenos Aires province, reunified with the Confederation (Cliopatria's 1861 shape minus its 1857 shape)

ledger.note: 12 December 1861: Buenos Aires returns after Pavon. Mitre defeated Urquiza at Pavon on 17 September 1861 and the infobox gives 'Reunification: 12 December 1861'; Buenos Aires province comes back to the Confederation.

December 1861: the Confederation becomes the Republic of Argentina. The page says Buenos Aires returned to the Confederation, which then became the Republic of Argentina (infobox: succeeded by the Argentine Republic in 1861). Colour and dossier continue.

1862: the national government returns to Buenos Aires (page silent on the year: the Provinces of Argentina page has only that the city 'was made a federal territory in 1880' and an 1862 law on national territories).

region.text: the city of Corrientes and San Cosme, taken by Paraguay on 13 April 1865

ledger.note: 13 April 1865: Paraguay takes Corrientes. 'Following the invasion of the Corrientes Province by Paraguay on 13 April 1865'; the Treaty of the Triple Alliance was signed on 1 May 1865 by Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.

region.text: the city of Corrientes and San Cosme

ledger.note: 1866: Corrientes is cleared. The page says only that 'In subsequent months, the Paraguayans were driven out of the cities of Corrientes and San Cosme' (no date; the year follows the Paraguay dossier).

region.text: Formosa and Misiones

region.text: Neuquen Province up to the Limay River

region.text: Tierra del Fuego east of 68°34' W and Staten Island

ledger.note: 23 July 1881: Tierra del Fuego is divided with Chile. The treaty 'was signed on 23 July 1881 in Buenos Aires'; the dividing line runs 'along the meridian 68°34' west of Greenwich', the eastern side going to Argentina, and 'to the Argentine Republic shall belong Staten Island'.

region.text: Patagonia east of the Andean watershed, south to 52 S

ledger.note: 23 July 1881: the Andes line fixes Argentine Patagonia. Article 1 runs the border 'over the highest summits of the said Cordilleras which divide the waters' down to 52 S, leaving the Atlantic side to Argentina; the page does not name Santa Cruz, so the province is the researcher's reading, and the Argentine occupation dates from the 1881-1884 campaigns.

region.text: Rio Negro and Chubut, the last Indigenous land of northern Patagonia

ledger.note: 18 October 1884: the last battle of the Conquest of the Desert. 'The last battle' was on 18 October 1884 and the chieftains Inacayal and Foyel surrendered 'two months later in present Chubut Province'; the page names Chubut but gives no list of what else fell.

region.text: the Puna de Atacama, disputed between Bolivia, Chile and Argentina

ledger.note: 1899: the Puna de Atacama lawsuit. 'The Puna de Atacama dispute was resolved by the Puna de Atacama Lawsuit of 1899. Its cause lay in land transfers between Bolivia and Argentina.' The page names the dispute, not the line; Chile also claimed the Puna. Cliopatria's shape holds the Puna already, so no cell changes.

region.text: the whole Argentine state of 1929, handed to Cliopatria's Argentine Republic row

ledger.note: 1929: Cliopatria's Argentine Confederation row ends and its Argentine Republic row begins in 1930. This is a row boundary, not a state's end: the same land continues as the Argentine Republic (the Argentine Confederation page itself ends in 1861).

wars.name: Rosas's expedition of 1833 (Conquest of the Desert)
wars.outcome: A partial success on the Buenos Aires frontier: 'only Rosas's expedition achieved some success'.
wars.note: The page gives no 1834 date and no line.

wars.name: Confederation-Buenos Aires war (Cepeda 1859, Pavon 1861)
wars.outcome: Urquiza's Confederation beat Mitre at Cepeda (23 October 1859); Mitre beat Urquiza at Pavon (17 September 1861) and Buenos Aires returned to the Confederation on 12 December 1861, which became the Republic of Argentina.
wars.note: The Pact of San Jose de Flores (November 1859) is named only in a reference title on the page.

wars.name: Paraguayan War

zones.text: the lands south of the Pilcomayo and Misiones

wars.outcome: The Triple Alliance won: Solano Lopez died at Cerro Cora on 1 March 1870; Argentine and Brazilian troops occupied Paraguay until 1876 and the Machain-Irigoyen Treaty (3 February 1876) gave Argentina Misiones and Formosa.
wars.note: Paraguay 'permanently lost its claims to lands amounting to almost 40%' of its prewar claims (the page also says about 30 percent). The Hayes award (no date on the page) left the Chaco Central to Paraguay.

wars.name: War of the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
wars.outcome: The Confederation fell at Yungay on 20 January 1839 and was dissolved in 1839. Argentina 'declared war on the Confederation on 19 May 1837'; no border moved for Argentina.
wars.note: The Bolivia page gives 9 May 1837 for the declaration.

wars.name: Conquest of the Desert

zones.text: La Pampa, Neuquen, Rio Negro, Chubut and Patagonia

wars.outcome: Argentina took the Pampas and northern Patagonia: Roca's sweeps of 1878-1879 reached the Rio Negro, Villegas took Neuquen in 1881 and the last battle was on 18 October 1884; the chiefs surrendered in Chubut two months later.
wars.note: The page gives no area in km2 and no Santa Cruz or Tierra del Fuego dates; those come from the 1881 treaty.

wars.name: Uruguayan Civil War (Guerra Grande)
wars.outcome: Rosas, governor of Buenos Aires, would not recognise Rivera and sought to restore Oribe, whose forces combined with his and besieged Montevideo from 1843; Oribe was defeated in 1851 after Urquiza's uprising against Rosas and Brazil's May 1851 intervention. No Argentine border moved.
wars.note: The page does not say the Argentine Confederation army took part as such; it describes the combined forces of Rosas and Oribe.

certainty.note: The frontier with Indigenous land (Pampas, Patagonia, Chaco) is approximate; the Paraguayan line is sharp from 3 February 1876.
The Chilean line is fixed by the treaty of 23 July 1881; the Chaco and the Bolivian Puna frontier stay soft.
The Puna de Atacama lawsuit of 1899 and the 1902 arbitration settle the northern and Chilean lines; the Chaco and Misiones frontiers are treaty lines.

notes:
Nine pages opened for this dossier (the budget is nine) plus the Peru-Bolivian Confederation and Uruguayan Civil War pages opened for the Bolivia and Uruguay dossiers. A fetch of 'National Territories of Argentina' failed (URL not found) and was replaced by 'Provinces of Argentina', which gives only the 1862 law, the 1880 federal territory and the 1884 governorates.

ONE STATE, TWO ROWS: Cliopatria's 'Argentine Confederation' row (1834-1929) is the Argentine state throughout, not the 1831-1861 Confederation the Wikipedia article describes (Disestablished 1861, 'succeeded by the Argentine Republic'). The Argentine Republic row (1930-2024, slug argentine-republic, Wikipedia 'Argentina') is the same state on the same land; the dissolve event at 1929 is only a row boundary. The colour agent should give both one colour (rename events carry the change of name). The end year 1929 and the successor are Cliopatria's, not history's.

OVERLAP WITH RIO DE LA PLATA: the Confederation dates from the Federal Pact of 4 January 1831 (infobox), so this dossier starts in 1831 and adds a new keyframe for 1831-1833 (Rio de la Plata's 1833 shape, identical to its 1830-1833 shape). The Rio de la Plata dossier also draws those years (dissolve at 1833). One of them must yield: either end Rio de la Plata in 1830 or start the Confederation in 1834.

CLAIMS IN THE SHAPE: from 1834 the shape holds the Argentine Chaco (433 of 460 cells) and Misiones (111 of 128 cells).
